## ES round synthesis: 22 pre-registered variants, 6 families, nothing nominated, nothing replicated, nothing confirmed

**Bottom line.** Zero of the 22 variants met the pre-registered survivor bar (mean_net > 0, t >= 2.5, n >= 150, net P&L > 0 in >= 8 of the 13 in-sample calendar years 2005-2017). `SURVIVORS: []`, `VERDICTS: []`, and all six family result files (`/home/user/j/research/hyp/es_*_results.json`) carry `survivors: []`. Because nothing was nominated, the holdout-replication lens and the audit lens were never exercised: there are no holdout runs, no audit reports, and `research/verify/` is empty. "Confirmed by both lenses" is the empty set, and so is "confirmed by either lens". Nothing feeds the Topstep dynamic program from this round. The sealed holdout (`data_research/HO`, 2018-01-01 .. 2020-05, 29 months) was not opened by any of the six scripts (each hard-codes `ROOT = data_research/IS`; verified by grep), so it remains clean for a later round.

**Trial accounting.** 5 + 4 + 4 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 22 variants, matching the task header; every family deflated its Sharpe with N = 22, which is the right count for this dataset (the 211 earlier crypto trials were on unrelated data). Note, however, that four of the six families (intraday momentum, ORB, VWAP reversion, calendar) are re-registrations on a new asset of ideas that already failed on BTC/ETH; that is legitimate pre-registration, but it means the ES families were not chosen blind. It changes nothing today: the best DSR with n >= 150 is 0.59 and the best t with n >= 150 is 2.17.

**Data and proxy caveat (applies to every number below).** All results are on the Oanda SPX500 CFD 1-minute series (bars only when the quote changed, tick volume, no roll/basis) with ES economics bolted on ($50/pt, $16.28 round turn = $3.78 commission + one tick slippage). The CFD is a spot-index proxy, not the futures; for the overnight and FOMC families the CFD's financing/dividend adjustment and the futures basis roll are not the same thing, so a per-night drift of a few dollars is within the proxy error. 3,311,533 bars 2005-01-02..2017-12-29, ~3,234 days with a valid 14:30 CT fill.

### Family-by-family: what was found, what was nominated, what the lenses said

| Family | Variants | Best in-sample variant | n | net $/ES | t | DSR | pos. yrs | trades/day | Nominated | Replication | Audit | Confirmed (both) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| intraday_momentum | 5 | V5 first-60-min sign -> last 30 min | 3158 | -8.74 | -2.15 | ~0 | 4/13 | 0.93 | none | not run | not run | none |
| overnight_drift | 4 | V2 long 17:00->08:30 after a down cash day | 1136 | +9.29 | 0.74 | 0.12 | 9/13 | 0.34 | none | not run | not run | none |
| orb_continuation | 4 | V2 30-min ORB, wide-range filter | 1525 | -14.01 | -1.02 | 0.00 | 5/13 | 0.45 | none | not run | not run | none |
| fomc_drift | 3 | V1 long 17:00 day-before -> 12:55 statement day | 102 | +125.19 | 2.88 | 0.82 | 8/13 | 0.03 | none (n < 150) | not run | not run | none |
| calendar_flows | 3 | V1 turn-of-month long, 4 legs | 603 | +7.79 | 0.26 | 0.05 | 7/13 | 0.18 | none | not run | not run | none |
| vwap_reversion | 3 | V3 0.30% band, low-range days | 3135 | -25.57 | -7.00 | ~0 | 1/13 | 0.93 | none | not run | not run | none |

All stored JSON values were re-read and match the task text to the cent; "pos. yrs" was recomputed from each variant's `by_year` and agrees.

**intraday_momentum (5 variants, all negative net).** First-30/first-60-minute sign and 14:00->14:30 sign into the 14:30->15:08 CT window, with and without a 60-day z-filter and a both-agree filter. Every variant is negative net (t from -2.15 to -3.92, at most 4/13 positive years) and the gross means are essentially zero (+0.41, -3.38, +0.01, +1.03, +7.54 $/contract): there is no momentum to buy and no reversal to sell, only the round turn. The direct correlation of the 14:30->15:08 return with the first-half-hour return is -0.051 (t = -2.9), the opposite sign to the Gao-Han-Li-Zhou result that motivated the family; the 14:00->14:30 signal has rho = +0.133 (t = 7.6) but sign agreement is 47.6% and the linear relation lives in the 2008 tails, which a sign rule cannot capture. NAS100/NQ twin and the alternative timing convention give the same null. Nothing nominated; lenses not exercised; confirmed: none.

**overnight_drift (4 variants, the one weakly positive family).** Long 17:00 CT -> 08:30 CT next day (V1), the same after a down cash day (V2), to 09:00 (V3), and the short day-session mirror (V4). The overnight premium exists on the proxy but is tiny: gross +$18.0 per night (0.36 ES pt) for V1 and +$25.6 for V2, which the $16.28 round turn consumes (net +1.77 and +9.29, t 0.24 and 0.74). V2 is the best thing in the whole round with n >= 150 (9/13 positive years, DSR 0.12) and it is nowhere near t = 2.5; its per-trade standard deviation is $421 per ES contract, so a $9 mean is 2% of one sigma. The short-day leg V4 is significantly negative (t = -3.04, 3/13 years, -$96k per contract over 13 years) because the 09:00->15:08 day session was itself positive on this proxy: the anomaly's premise (flat or negative day session) does not hold at these boundaries. The NQ twin is relatively stronger (V1 t = 2.11, 11/13 years) but still fails t. Precision note: the early-close/reopen exit rule (Good Friday, holiday half-days, where the protocol's 15:10 forced flat cannot fire because there are no bars) was added after an initial run showed 4 V1 trades riding a weekend; the committed pre-fix JSON had V1 n = 3281, mean +1.55, t = 0.21 and V4 mean -28.09, t = -2.97, so the post-P&L fix moved V1 by +$0.22 and V4 by -$0.67 and changed no verdict, but it is a post-hoc implementation change and should be recorded as such. Nothing nominated; lenses not exercised; confirmed: none.

**orb_continuation (4 variants, all negative net).** 30- and 60-minute cash-open range breakouts with the opposite range side as stop, flat at 15:08 CT or after 2 hours, with and without a width filter. All four are negative net and V1/V4 significantly so (t = -2.72, -5.39); gross means are -5.0, +2.3, +1.6, -9.4 $/contract, so the cash-open breakout simply does not continue on average 2005-2017, costs or no costs. 2008 is the lone big positive year for V1-V3 (crisis trend days); 10-12 of 13 years are negative. The width filter is the least bad (t = -1.02, CI spans zero) and still far from the bar. The engine was cross-checked trade by trade against `protocol.backtest_signals` (only touch-only stop-level ulp differences, 37/18/33/14 outcomes per variant). Nothing nominated; lenses not exercised; confirmed: none.

**fomc_drift (3 variants, the only t > 2.5 in the round, and it cannot qualify).** Long the evening before each scheduled FOMC statement into 12:55 CT (V1), the two-evening version (V2), and post-announcement continuation 13:36->15:08 (V3). V1 clears mean, t and years (mean +$125, t = 2.88, 8/13) but has n = 102 against a bar of 150; with only 104 scheduled statements in 13 years, a one-trade-per-event rule can never reach the n bar in-sample, so V1 and V3 were structurally unnominable from the start. Three further reasons to be skeptical of V1 beyond the n bar: (i) the effect is concentrated in 2007-2009 and the 13:15-CT-release era (n = 55, mean +$219, t = 3.56) and is absent in the 13:00 era 2013-2017 (n = 39, mean -$35, t = -0.54), i.e. invisible in the last five in-sample years; (ii) the pre-registration's assumed release time was wrong for the eight 2011-2012 press-conference meetings (statements came at 11:30 CT, not 13:30), so the registered 12:55 exit held those eight trades 85 minutes post-announcement; implemented literally as registered, they contributed mean +$261, and with the corrected 11:25 exit V1 falls to mean +$105, t = 2.42, DSR 0.68, i.e. below the t bar as well; (iii) the NQ twin is much weaker (t = 1.60). V2 (n = 205) fails on t = 2.17 (DSR 0.59; corrected t = 1.95) and V3 is negative. The holdout holds 18 scheduled statements (8 + 8 + 2020-01-29 and 2020-04-29; the March 2020 emergency cuts are unscheduled and excluded by the rule), far too few to test anything at t >= 2 even if V1 had been nominated. Announcement dates were parsed from the saved Fed pages for 2005-2019; 2020 could not be parsed (the saved calendar page holds 2021-2027 only) and a labelled fallback list is in the script, unused. Nothing nominated; lenses not exercised; confirmed: none.

**calendar_flows (3 variants).** Turn-of-month long over four 17:00->15:08 legs (V1: +$7.79, t = 0.26, 7/13; the month-end T-1 leg is the worst at -$51.6), month-end last-hour long (V2), and third-Friday fade (V3: -$3.13, t = -0.13, all positive P&L from 2008). V2 is the one strong signal in the family and it is the wrong sign: -$88.73 per trade, t = -3.94, negative in 12 of 13 years, bootstrap CI [-131.9, -45.6], gross -$72.45, and the NQ twin is also negative (t = -2.45). The opposite side was not pre-registered and cannot be nominated. For the record, the arithmetic mirror from the stored stats (not a run) would be: short net = +72.45 - 16.28 = +$56.17, t = +2.49, n = 149, so even the mirrored short would miss the bar on t by 0.01 and on n by one trade, and at 0.044 trades/day (11 trades a year) it would be useless for a Topstep combine regardless. It is a legitimate candidate for a future pre-registered short variant, nothing more. Nothing nominated; lenses not exercised; confirmed: none.

**vwap_reversion (3 variants, the worst family).** Fade 0.20%/0.30% excursions from the cash-session VWAP back to VWAP with a symmetric stop, with and without a low-range-day filter. All three lose before costs (gross -8.3 / -5.4 / -9.3 $/contract); stops are hit ~1.8x as often as the VWAP target; V1 and V2 are negative in every year 2005-2016 (t = -9.74, -14.47); re-entries after stops compound losses on trend days (up to 39 trades in a day). The loss is symmetric by side (long t = -7.28, short t = -6.48), so it is not a drift artefact. The NQ twin is the same. Nothing nominated; lenses not exercised; confirmed: none.

### What the round says collectively

- Of 22 variants, 15 are negative net, 4 are positive but indistinguishable from zero (overnight V1/V2/V3, turn-of-month V1; t <= 0.74), and 3 are FOMC variants where the only t above 2.5 sits on n = 102 and shrinks to 2.42 once the pre-registration's release-time error is corrected. Highest t with n >= 150: 2.17. Highest DSR with n >= 150: 0.59.
- Two families (VWAP reversion, ORB continuation) and the month-end last hour lose *gross*, so the finding is not just "costs ate the edge": the intraday mean-reversion-to-VWAP premise and the cash-open continuation premise are false on this proxy in 2005-2017, and the intraday-momentum premise is absent (gross ~ $0).
- The two anomalies that exist on the proxy (overnight premium, pre-FOMC drift) are either too small for one ES round turn (overnight: 0.36 pt per night gross) or too rare and era-dependent (FOMC: ~8 events a year, edge gone after 2012 in-sample).
- Per-trade dollar volatility on one ES contract is $230-$730 (sd = mean*sqrt(n)/t: intraday momentum $229, overnight $420, FOMC V1 $439, turn-of-month $731). Against a Topstep 50K daily loss limit of $1,000 that is 1.4-4 sigma per trade on a single contract; any ES rule that ever does pass would have to be priced in MES, and MES net is not ES net / 10 (MES round turn $2.47 is relatively 1.5x more expensive per point than ES's $16.28): MES net = ES gross / 10 - 2.47. `evaluate_survivor.evaluate()` also rounds trades/day to max(1, round(tpd)), so event-frequency rules (0.03-0.18 trades/day) would be modelled at 5-30x their true frequency; that needs fixing before any such rule is ever priced.

### The holdout: 2.4 years with three stress episodes, and how that cuts both ways

The sealed holdout is 2018-01-01 .. 2020-05 (last source file `oanda-SPX500_USD-2020-5.csv`): 29 months, about 606 NYSE trading days, containing the February 2018 volatility spike, the October-December 2018 drawdown and the February-March 2020 crash. (The repo does not define the three episodes anywhere; these are the obvious three from the calendar, not from the data.)

It cuts against false positives, which is the point: a rule tuned to the 2009-2017 calm regime that only looks good because it was never stressed would fail there, and three episodes of opposite character (a vol-product unwind, a slow Q4 bear, a liquidity crash) are a harsher regime test than most 2.4-year windows. For a Topstep evaluation, where pass probability is driven by the loss tail and the daily/trailing limits, stress-period behaviour is exactly the information the DP needs; a calm-period holdout confirmation would say little about what matters.

It also cuts against true positives, and more sharply than the stress count suggests. An edge sitting exactly on the IS bar (t = 2.5 over ~3200 trades) has a per-trade Sharpe of 0.044; over ~580 holdout trades its expected t is 1.06, so P(t_HO >= 2) is about 0.17 and P(mean_HO > 0) about 0.86. The arithmetic is the same for every frequency class (IS t = 2.5 at any n gives E[t_HO] ~ 1.05 for a holdout 0.19x the IS length): a holdout confirmation rule of t >= 2 would reject a genuine bar-level edge five times in six, and the stress episodes make it worse by roughly doubling per-trade variance in those months (the 2008 analogue in-sample: intraday momentum V1 lost $10.6k in 2008 alone against $1-5k in normal years). Conversely, the episodes make a false positive easier to manufacture: 2008 was the *only* positive year for ORB V1-V3 and intraday momentum V3, so a trend-following rule that is null in-sample could print a positive holdout purely on March 2020. Two practical consequences: (a) holdout verdicts in this programme should be read as sign-and-magnitude replication (mean > 0, within the IS CI, no single-episode dominance) rather than as an independent t >= 2 test, and (b) with 3 episodes in 29 months, any holdout mean, positive or negative, carries a wide interval dominated by those months, so neither a pass nor a fail there would be a strong statement. Both halves argue for not spending the holdout on anything that has not cleared the in-sample bar with room to spare, which is what happened.

### Housekeeping and things to fix before another ES round

1. Five of the six family scripts and JSONs are untracked and `es_overnight_drift.py` / its JSON are modified relative to commit f060600 (the early-close fix); the raw results should be committed as-is with the post-P&L fix noted.
2. The survivor bar's n >= 150 structurally excludes one-trade-per-event families on 13 years of data (104 FOMC statements, 156 month-ends, 156 third Fridays). Either register multi-leg or multi-event versions, or decide up front that such families are diagnostics, not candidates.
3. The FOMC pre-registration carried a factual error (13:30 CT assumed for 2011-2012 press-conference releases; the data show 11:30 CT). The registered rule was run literally and the corrected version reported as a diagnostic, which is the right handling, but release-time facts should be checked against the data before the next registration, since here the error flattered the headline t by 0.46.
4. `overnight_drift` and `fomc_drift` JSONs omit the `survivor_bar` field that the other four carry; harmless, but the files should share one schema.
5. The DP feed in `research/evaluate_survivor.py` expects per-micro-contract stats and integer trades/day; the ES round produces per-ES-contract stats at fractional frequencies, so a conversion step (MES cost model, event-frequency handling) is needed before anything from this programme can be priced.

### Stats for the Topstep dynamic program

None. No variant was confirmed by either lens, so there is no per-trade $, trades/day, n, win rate or avg win/loss to hand to the DP. The in-sample figures in the table above are reported for the record only and must not be used as DP inputs.
